diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\int_Dn_{p^\star}'\left|w_{p^\star}\right|^2\neq 0$, with $n_{p^\star}'$ denoting the derivative of $p\mapsto n_p$ at $p=p^\star$
provide simple, practical criteria to verify the local smoothness of real ITP eigenpair trajectories

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence claims a complete biconditional diagnostic from the single test I(p)=0. The paper's sufficient condition (cor:bifurc, inheriting thm:bifurc's hypotheses) additionally requires the nondegeneracy hypothesis quoted above, which is not implied by I(p*)=0: e.g., for a stationary parametrization (n_p constant in p) of the unit disk at a configuration with J_m(κ*)=J_m(p₀κ*)=0, the constant (perfectly smooth) real trajectory has I≡0 and ∫n_p'|w_p|²=0, so the check gives a false positive. Conversely, the check can give false negatives: removable exceptional points (non-smoothly relabeled trajectories at smooth crossings, a phenomenon explicitly discussed in Sec. 3) are exceptional points with I≠0. The conclusions' claim of criteria to "verify the local smoothness" overstates in the same way, since the necessity direction is only available under cor:bifurc_sufficient's extra hypotheses (analytic n_p, one-sided realness, integer bifurcation order).

The proof derives only the undivided identity κ_pκ_p'I(p)=½κ_p²∫n_p'|w_p|² and divides by I(p) without justification. Admissible inputs with I(p)=0 exist whenever ∫n_p'|w_p|²=0 as well: e.g., a constant-in-p parametrization n_p≡p₀² of the unit disk at a configuration with J_m(κ*)=J_m(p₀κ*)=0 (such p₀=j_{m,l}/j_{m,k}≠1 exist) gives a constant, hence continuously differentiable, real eigenpair trajectory with I≡0 and ∫n_p'|w_p|²≡0, for which the asserted right-hand side is the undefined quantity 0/0. issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims that every bifurcation involving a locally real eigenvalue occurs at a Bessel zero and is cubic. The proof computes the indicator on a one-sided-real branch (via rem:angle) but then only analyzes 'roots p* of I': it never establishes that the bifurcation point is such a root. The missing inference — that a bifurcation on a one-sided-real branch forces I(p*)=0 — is exactly the converse of cor:bifurc_sufficient, which the paper proves (its hypotheses hold on the disk: analytic n_p≡p², ∫n'|w|²≠0 by lem:nonzero, C¹ on a punctured neighborhood) but which the proof does not invoke. As written, the argument establishes only the materially weaker statement 'roots of I are Bessel zeros and produce cubic bifurcations'.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right
The table displays the rate $\alpha$ such that $\overline{I}(p)\sim-|p-p^\star|^\alpha$

issues.failure_explanation: For the unit disk with p>1, the paper's own formula I=(a_mπ/2)(1−p²)J_m(κ_p)² combined with (eq:ind_simpl) gives \bar I=J_m(κ_p)²≥0 on real trajectories (strictly positive away from Bessel zeros, for any eigenfunction normalization), yet the text asserts the displayed indicator is strictly negative there and the captions state \bar I∼−|p−p*|^α. For the annulus (n_p=p², p>1, κ>0), lem:bifurc_ord gives sign(κ_p')=sign(I)=−sign(\bar I), so \bar I is positive exactly for trajectories traveling LEFT; the text claims the opposite ('positive if and only if ... traveling to the right'), attributing it to cor:bifurc, which states nothing about signs. The sign of the indicator described in the narrative (and in the captions of fig:disk:fit, fig:annulus:fit, and the statements that the disk indicator is 'uniformly non-positive') matches I (equivalently −\bar I), not \bar I as defined; the definition and the entire numerical sign narrative cannot both be correct.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: exploiting the realness of Bessel functions for real inputs
Let $\kappa\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}$ be a \emph{non-real} eigenvalue with eigenfunction pair $(v,w)\in[L^2(D)]^2$.
a real (piecewise-smooth) eigenvalue trajectory undergoes bifurcation if and only if $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition imposes no realness restriction on the eigenpair trajectory, but its proof applies the Bessel-product integral identity (eq:integral_sum) — derived 'exploiting the realness of Bessel functions for real inputs' — after the changes of variables x=κρ and x=pκρ, which are valid only when κ (hence pκ) is real. For non-real eigenvalues the computation is invalid. Moreover, by lem:zeronorm, I(p)=0 (hence \bar I=0) for every non-real eigenvalue, so the stated identity would force ‖v_p‖_{L^∞(∂B_1)}=r‖v_p‖_{L^∞(∂B_r)} for all non-real annulus eigenpairs — an identity nothing in the source supports (and contradicted in the r→0⁺ limit by the disk, where non-real ITEs satisfy J_m(κ)≠0 since zeros of J_m are real). The proposition is therefore unproven, and evidently false, on the non-real regime; all its actual uses (the 'immediate consequence', rem:annulus:ord, the numerics) concern real trajectories.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to eigenpair trajectories with real eigenvalue κ_p, for which the proof is valid and the formula holds.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition, one of the paper's stated annulus contributions, is unreliable for non-real eigenvalue trajectories — precisely the trajectories displayed in the annulus experiments; applying the formula there yields wrong indicator values.
issues.title: prop:annulus:bifurc_ord asserted for all eigenpair trajectories but valid only for real eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase hypothesis addition repairs the proposition; every downstream use is already real-only, and on the excluded non-real regime the indicator is identically zero by lem:zeronorm, so no usable content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: By polar separability, v=V(ρ)φ(mθ) with sup|φ|=1, so the proposition's bifurcation condition reads |V(1)|=r|V(r)|, while the boundary L² norms include the arc-length factor: ‖v‖²_{L²(∂B_ρ)}=ρ·a_mπ·|V(ρ)|². Hence the stated L² condition ‖v‖_{L²(∂B_1)}=‖v‖_{L²(∂B_r)} is equivalent to |V(1)|=√r|V(r)|, which differs from |V(1)|=r|V(r)| for every r≠1 (e.g., r=0.1: √r≈0.316 vs r=0.1). The claimed equivalence is false; the correct equivalent condition is ‖v‖_{L²(∂B_1)}=√r‖v‖_{L²(∂B_r)} (equivalently, equality of squared norms with a factor r).

issues.overall_effect: The L² reformulation of the annulus bifurcation criterion, as stated, gives a wrong condition; it is not used elsewhere in the paper.
